product_family: CodeQL is a semantic code analysis engine that enables security researchers and developers to discover vulnerabilities across codebases. It powers GitHub Advanced Security's code scanning and is available as a free tool for research and open source, or as a paid feature for enterprises.

certifications.name: SOC 2 Type II
certifications.proof_quote: GitHub maintains up-to-date, official SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 compliance reports available through organization settings for eligible organizations.

certifications.name: ISO/IEC 27001:2022
certifications.proof_quote: GitHub holds ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification, which demonstrates its commitment to information security management standards.

certifications.name: CSA CAIQ (Cloud Security Alliance CAIQ)
certifications.proof_quote: GitHub provides Cloud Security Alliance CAIQ self-assessment (CSA CAIQ - Level 1) compliance reports accessible through organization settings.

certifications.name: CSA STAR Level 2
certifications.proof_quote: GitHub holds Cloud Security Alliance STAR certification (CSA STAR - Level 2).

certifications.name: PCI DSS
certifications.proof_quote: GitHub maintains PCI DSS Attestation of Compliance as part of its security certifications portfolio.

certifications.name: GDPR
certifications.proof_quote: GitHub's privacy statement (effective April 27, 2026) establishes data processing, user rights, and retention policies compliant with GDPR. GitHub commits to responding to data access/deletion requests within 45 days.

certifications.name: HIPAA
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of GitHub-provided Business Associate Agreement (BAA) or HIPAA compliance program for CodeQL or GitHub services. Search results show community HIPAA templates but no official GitHub BAA.

certifications.name: FedRAMP
certifications.proof_quote: No evidence of FedRAMP certification in GitHub's public compliance documentation. GitHub maintains SOC 2, ISO 27001, CSA CAIQ, CSA STAR, and PCI DSS, but FedRAMP is not listed.

certifications.name: ISO 42001 (AI Governance)
certifications.proof_quote: No public evidence of ISO/IEC 42001:2023 certification for AI systems governance.

privacy.ai_training_note: GitHub's Terms of Service (as of 2026) explicitly state that GitHub may use inputs and outputs to train AI models. This applies to content in public repositories. Users can opt out via account settings. Private repositories are protected from general AI training but may be accessed for security, support, legal compliance, or malware detection.
privacy.data_region: GitHub operates data centers with processing in multiple regions. Private repositories are generally stored in the user's selected region.

security.name: Encryption in transit
security.value: GitHub uses TLS/HTTPS for all connections; stated as 'secure with ISO, SOC 2, and GDPR'

security.name: Data Retention
security.value: GitHub retains personal data as long as accounts remain active and for legal compliance purposes.

security.name: Security Incident Response
security.value: GitHub maintains a Security Incident Response Team (SIRT) per RFC 2350 standard.

security.name: Bug Bounty Program
security.value: GitHub operates a bug bounty program with legal safe harbor for authorized security researchers.

security.name: Subprocessors
security.value: GitHub maintains a public list of subprocessors. Includes affiliates (Microsoft), service providers, and law enforcement when legally required.

products.name: CodeQL (Free/Community)
products.data_scope: Open source codebases and academic research only
products.notes: Free for research and open source. Requires OSI-approved license or academic use. Downloadable via CLI. User must agree to GitHub CodeQL Terms & Conditions.

products.name: CodeQL (GitHub Advanced Security)
products.notes: Part of GitHub Advanced Security for enterprise customers. Includes code scanning in CI/CD, no restrictions on codebase type.

products.name: CodeQL (VS Code Extension)
products.notes: IDE integration for querying CodeQL databases. Free for open source; paid license required for commercial use on private code.

compare.pricing_model: Freemium: Free for open source and research; subscription-based for enterprise (part of GitHub Advanced Security pricing)
compare.data_residency: GitHub stores data in the customer's selected region when available; enterprise customers may negotiate data processing locations

flags: CodeQL does not hold separate certifications; it inherits GitHub's certifications as a GitHub product. This is appropriate and not a deficiency.
AI training on public repo content is enabled by default. Users must explicitly opt out via GitHub account settings. Private repositories are protected.
HIPAA compliance: GitHub does not appear to offer a BAA for HIPAA compliance. Organizations handling PHI should not use CodeQL without explicit legal review.
FedRAMP: Not certified. Federal agencies should verify GitHub/CodeQL compliance with FedRAMP or equivalent before deployment.
Licensing: Free CodeQL usage is strictly limited to open source and research. Commercial use on closed-source code requires GitHub Advanced Security subscription.
